## Introduction

**Goal:** Optimize the NetC14 hyperparameter $\gamma$ - the weight on the
precision penalty - with respect to the held-out likelihood of radiocarbon
samples. Because this criterion uses only the observed samples, it can also be
computed on real data where the true ages and density are unknown. The sparsemax
temperature $\pi$ is fixed at 1, since it overlaps with $\gamma$ in promoting
sparsity, and tuning both leaves the optimum poorly identified.

**Data:** For model tuning, data are simulated according to the generative
model.

**Method:** We sweep a fixed grid of $\gamma$ values against a fixed panel of
simulated chronologies, scoring every value against the same set of
chronologies to focus on variance across values. Samples in
each chronology are split into five folds. Each configuration is fit to four
folds and scored by the log marginal likelihood of the fifth, rotating through
all five.

## Data

```{r}
#| label: intcal20

intcal20 <- structure(
  read.csv("data/intcal20.csv"),
  class = c("Calibration", "data.frame"),
  curve = "IntCal20"
)

intcal20 <- intcal20 |>
  transform(f14c_mu = exp(-c14_age / LIBBY)) |>
  transform(f14c_sigma = f14c_mu * c14_error / LIBBY)
```

## Tuning

The chronology grid crosses problem size, sample count, mixture complexity, and
component distribution scenarios. Every value of $\gamma$ is evaluated against
every chronological scenario. Note that $\gamma$ is multiplicative, so we use a
log-spaced grid, so we are looking at something like the elasticity of NLL 
relative to this hyperparameter.

```{r}
#| label: tuning-grid
gammas <- 2^seq(-2, 6, by = 0.5)

evaluation_grid <- expand.grid(
  n_years = c(500, 2500, 12500),
  n_samples = c(50, 250, 1250),
  n_clusters = c(1, 3, 9),
  distribution = c("gaussian", "uniform", "skewed"),
  replicate = seq_len(2),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

n_scenarios <- nrow(evaluation_grid)
```

Each worker process runs one scenario at a time: it simulates the chronology,
draws and calibrates samples, splits them into folds, and then sweeps every
value of $\gamma$ against those same folds.

```{r}
#| label: tuning-loop
#| cache: true
#| output: false
#| time_it: true
clusters <- makeCluster(12)

fns <- c(
  "calibrate.R",
  "constants.R",
  "dataframe-helpers.R",
  "mixture-helpers.R",
  "netc14.R",
  "sample-dates.R",
  "simulate-chronology.R",
  "spd.R"
)

clusterExport(
  clusters,
  varlist = c("fns", "intcal20", "gammas", "evaluation_grid"),
  envir = environment()
)

clusterEvalQ(clusters, {
  library(torch)
  torch_set_num_threads(1)
  lapply(file.path("R", fns), source, verbose = FALSE)
})

# run simulations in parallel, one scenario at a time
tuning_results <- parLapplyLB(clusters, seq_len(n_scenarios), \(i) {
  set.seed(STARGATE + (1000 * i))

  # scenario
  n_years <- evaluation_grid[["n_years"]][i]
  n_clusters <- evaluation_grid[["n_clusters"]][i]
  n_samples <- evaluation_grid[["n_samples"]][i]
  distribution <- evaluation_grid[["distribution"]][i]
  start <- sample(seq(100, 49500 - n_years), 1)
  end <- start + n_years - 1

  # simulate chronology, draw samples, and calibrate
  chronology <- simulate_chronology(start, end, n_clusters, distribution)
  samples <- sample_dates(chronology, n_samples, intcal20)
  calibrated_dates <- calibrate(samples, intcal20)

  # k-fold
  folds <- split(seq_len(n_samples), sample(rep_len(1:5, n_samples)))
  results <- vector("list", length(gammas))

  for (k in seq_along(gammas)) {
    heldout <- 0
    n_active <- c()

    for (fold in folds) {
      mdl <- netc(calibrated_dates[-fold, ], gamma = gammas[k], pi = 1)
      ll <- logLik(mdl, calibrated_dates[fold, , drop = FALSE])
      heldout <- heldout + ll
      n_active <- c(n_active, count_components(mdl))
    }

    results[[k]] <- cbind(
      scenario = i,
      gamma = gammas[k],
      evaluation_grid[i, ],
      start = start,
      nll = -sum(heldout) / n_samples,
      n_active = mean(n_active)
    )
  }

  do.call(rbind, results)
})

# close parallel processes and collect results
stopCluster(clusters)
tuning_results <- do.call(rbind, tuning_results)
```

Save results.

```{r}
#| label: save-results
write.csv(
  tuning_results,
  file = "data/tuning-results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Results

Held-out NLL is normalized within each scenario as the difference from the best
configuration for that scenario, so scenarios with different sample sizes and
intervals are comparable. Model complexity is measured as the ratio of active
to true components. We then choose $\gamma$ with the one-standard-error rule
(Hastie et al. 2017, section 7.10): the largest $\gamma$ whose mean held-out NLL
is no more than one standard error above the minimum.

```{r}
#| label: tuning-summary
tuning_results <- transform(
  tuning_results,
  nll = nll - ave(nll, scenario, FUN = min),
  ratio = n_active / n_clusters
)

tuning <- aggregate(
  cbind(nll, ratio) ~ gamma,
  data = tuning_results,
  FUN = mean
)

tuning[["se"]] <- aggregate(
  nll ~ gamma,
  data = tuning_results,
  FUN = \(x) sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
)[["nll"]]

i <- which.min(tuning[["nll"]])
threshold <- with(tuning, nll[i] + se[i])
best <- tuning[max(which(tuning[["nll"]] <= threshold)), ]

tuning[["threshold"]] <- threshold

write.csv(
  tuning,
  file = "data/tuning-summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: visualize-tuning-results
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false
x_ticks <- seq(-2, 6)
x_labels <- 2^x_ticks
xlim <- range(x_ticks)

xy <- transform(tuning, x = log2(gamma))
xy_best <- transform(best, x = log2(gamma))

svglite(
  "figures/tuning-objectives.svg",
  width = 7,
  height = 3
)

layout(matrix(1:2, nrow = 1))

par(defaults)
par(mai = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.1, 0.1))

with(xy, new_plot(xlim, range(nll - se, nll + se)))
add_grid(v = x_ticks)

with(
  xy,
  polygon(
    c(x, rev(x)),
    c(nll - se, rev(nll + se)),
    col = coolors("gray", shade = -0.8),
    border = NA
  )
)
abline(h = threshold, lty = "dashed", col = coolors("orange"))

with(xy, lines(x, nll, col = coolors("gray")))
with(xy, points(x, nll, pch = 19, col = coolors("gray")))
with(xy_best, points(x, nll, pch = 19, col = coolors("orange"), cex = 1.5))

x_axis(at = x_ticks, labels = x_labels)
y_axis()

x_label("Precision Penalty [γ]")
y_label("Held-out NLL [Δ]", line = 2.4)

with(xy, new_plot(xlim, range(1, ratio)))
add_grid(v = x_ticks)

abline(h = 1, lty = "dashed", col = coolors("gray"))

with(xy, lines(x, ratio, col = coolors("gray")))
with(xy, points(x, ratio, pch = 19, col = coolors("gray")))
with(xy_best, points(x, ratio, pch = 19, col = coolors("orange"), cex = 1.5))

x_axis(at = x_ticks, labels = x_labels)
y_axis()

x_label("Precision Penalty [γ]")
y_label("Active / True Components", line = 2.4)

dev.off()
```

![](/figures/tuning-objectives.svg){width=95%}
:::

### Scenario summary

The precision penalty should matter most where few samples are spread over a
long interval, so we also break held-out NLL down by interval length and sample
size.

```{r}
#| label: scenario-summary
scenario_summary <- aggregate(
  nll ~ gamma + n_years + n_samples,
  data = tuning_results,
  FUN = mean
)
```

```{r}
#| label: visualize-tuning-scenarios
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false
n_samples <- c(50, 250, 1250)
clrs <- coolors("yellow", "orange", "brown")

ylim <- range(scenario_summary[["nll"]])

widths <- c(2.05, 0.15, 1.65, 0.15, 1.65, 0.15, 0.7)

svglite(
  filename = "figures/tuning-scenarios.svg",
  width = sum(widths),
  height = 2.5,
  pointsize = 10
)

layout(matrix(c(1, 0, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4), nrow = 1), widths = widths)

par(defaults)

for (yrs in unique(scenario_summary[["n_years"]])) {
  xy_yrs <- scenario_summary[scenario_summary[["n_years"]] == yrs, ]

  par(mai = c(0.4, if (yrs == 500) 0.4 else 0, 0.25, 0))
  new_plot(xlim, ylim)
  add_grid(v = x_ticks)

  for (j in seq_along(n_samples)) {
    i <- which(xy_yrs[["n_samples"]] == n_samples[j])
    x <- log2(xy_yrs[["gamma"]][i])
    y <- xy_yrs[["nll"]][i]

    lines(x, y, col = clrs[j], lwd = 0.5)
    points(x, y, pch = 21, col = clrs[j], bg = coolors("gray", shade = -0.9))
  }

  x_axis(at = x_ticks, labels = x_labels)

  if (yrs == 2500) {
    x_label("Precision Penalty [γ]")
  }

  if (yrs == 500) {
    y_axis()
    y_label("Held-out NLL [Δ]")
  }

  main(paste(yrs, "Years"), col = coolors("gray"))
}

par(mai = rep(0, 4))
new_plot(c(0, 1), c(0, 1))
add_legend(
  x = 0.0,
  y = 0.7,
  legend = n_samples,
  col = clrs,
  text.col = clrs,
  pch = 21,
  pt.cex = 1.1,
  lwd = 0.5,
  title = "N Samples"
)

dev.off()
```

:::{#tuning-scenarios}
![](/figures/tuning-scenarios.svg){width=95%}
:::

### Optimal configuration

The selected $\gamma$ is highlighted in orange in the first figure above, with
the one-standard-error threshold shown as a dashed line.

```{r}
#| label: best-configuration
best
```
